To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the duration of face adaptation dissociates between different visual processes, and the ERP response reflects this dissociation.

(1) adaptation duration dissociates the category-, identity-, and image- specific processing steps, reflected in the N170, and P2 components, and (2) prolonged adaptation (3500 and/or 5000 ms duration) leads to the emergence of identity-specific processing steps, reflected on the P2 and N170 components.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms of human face perception and how they are modulated by the adaptation of the visual system.
the neural correlates of the face adaptation phenomenon, with a special focus on the dissociation of category, identity, and image-specific processes.
a new aspect of face adaptation, namely the dissociation of the category-, image-, and identity- specific processes by manipulating the adaptor duration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adaptation duration determines the degree of the dissociation among the category, identity-, image-specific processes.
prolonged adaptation leads to the enhancement of category-, image-, and identity-related processes in human face processing.

the duration of adaptation is a crucial factor in the modulation of category-, identity-, and image- specific processing steps of human face perception, and it can be used to study the neural correlates of the various stages of face processing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

rapid (200–3500 ms) adaptation is more likely to be associated with category-specific processing, while prolonged (5000–7000 ms) adaptation leads to the emergence of both identity- and image-specific processes as well.
the adaptation of different face processing steps is a dynamic process, and the duration of the adaptation determines the nature of the adaptation process.

the duration of adaptation plays a critical role in dissociating different face processing steps, which are reflected in the ERP signal.
